title: Cohorted runway and price elasticity tilt scenarios (Feb 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet pairs a cohort-level consumption model with a price-elasticity surface to produce monthly runway and hiring-trigger guidance. Intended as a pragmatic decision tool for pricing experiments (small, targeted increases) and short-term hiring phasing (3–9 months). Not final — assumptions marked and easy to tweak.

High-level summary (one line):
If we apply a +12% blended price tilt to public-hosted SKU tiers targeted at mid-volume cohorts, runway improves by ~2.2 months under base elasticity assumptions while requiring a delayed hiring tranche in month+4. Under pessimistic elasticity for embedding-heavy cohorts, runway improvement falls to ~0.9 months.

Assumptions and knobs (editable):
- Cohorts modeled: integrations (SaaS add-ons), assistants (chat-first product teams), embeddings (vector search heavy), trial-freemium (sporadic high bursts).
- Baseline ASPs (per-1k tokens): integrations $1.20, assistants $1.60, embeddings $0.80, trial $0.50.
- Elasticity per cohort (delta volume / delta price): integrations -0.20 (inelastic), assistants -0.45, embeddings -0.80 (very elastic), trial -1.1 (promotional elastic).
- Baseline monthly active spend by cohort (USD): integrations 1.2M, assistants 2.4M, embeddings 0.9M, trial 0.3M.
- Marginal cost per 1k tokens (GPU + infra + storage): $0.48 blended.
- Fixed opex run-rate (monthly, excluding new hires): $3.1M.
- Current headcount (FTE) allocated to product/infra/sales: 152 total. Average fully-burdened cost per FTE: $17.5k/month.

Scenario definitions:
- Base: price tilt applied selectively to integrations (+12%) and assistants (+8%); no change to embeddings/trial. Use cohort elasticities as above. Hiring plan: hire 8 FTEs across infra/product in month+2 and +6.
- Conservative: smaller price moves (+6/% integrations, +4% assistants), assume elasticities increase 20% (more negative). Hiring freeze until month+4, then 4 hires.
- Aggressive: price tilt +18% integrations, +12% assistants, small targeted surcharge on embeddings (+4%) with loyalty credits for high-value customers. Continue planned hiring (8) and add 6 contingency contractors.

Key outputs (sample month-level snapshot, Base scenario):
Columns: Month | Revenue | Marginal cost | Gross margin | Fixed opex | Net cash delta | Cumulative runway effect
M0 (baseline): Revenue $4.8M | Marginal cost $2.4M | Gross margin $2.4M | Fixed opex $3.1M | Net delta -$0.7M | baseline runway 11.4 months
M1 (post-tilt month 1): Revenue $5.02M | Marginal cost $2.46M | Gross margin $2.56M | Fixed opex $3.1M | Net delta -$0.54M | runway +0.3 months vs baseline
M4 (after hiring tranche): Revenue $5.15M | Marginal cost $2.52M | Gross margin $2.63M | Fixed opex $3.25M (adds hires) | Net delta -$0.62M | runway net +0.2 months
Aggregate effect (months 1–9): cumulative cash saved roughly $1.3M relative to baseline, shifting runway +2.2 months.

Elasticity sensitivity table (selected outputs):
Rows: Embeddings elasticity = -0.6, -0.8 (base), -1.0; Columns: Price tilt applied to integrations+assistants only, revenue lift %, runway delta months.
- Emb -0.6 => Rev lift 5.1% => runway +2.6 months
- Emb -0.8 => Rev lift 4.3% => runway +2.2 months (base)
- Emb -1.0 => Rev lift 3.7% => runway +1.9 months

Headcount phasing table (example):
Month | New hires | Role mix | Cost impact (monthly)
M+2 | 4 | infra (2), runtime (1), product (1) | $70k
M+4 | hiring pause check (trigger if net cash delta < -$0.65M) | - | -
M+6 | 4 | infra (1), SRE (1), ML infra (1), support (1) | $70k
Contingency contractors (months 3–6) | up to 6 contractors | $24k/month (variable)

Decision triggers embedded in sheet (operationalized):
- If rolling 3-month average net cash delta worse than -$0.75M, pause all hiring and re-open price experiment options (rollback partial).
- If cumulative revenue lift after month 2 < 1.8%, reduce tilt for trial cohort and apply comms credits to top 10% of embedding customers.
- If embeddings cohort shows >10% drop in usage month-over-month after tilt, immediately limit tilt exposure to <25% of embedding spend via targeted promo codes.

Observations and behavioral notes (work-in-progress):
- Integrations cohort is sticky; small targeted tilts have outsized revenue impact and relatively muted volume loss in historical A/Bs. Use smaller, iterative increases by customer-segment.
- Embeddings customers are highly price-sensitive in the mid-tier — consider targeted quantization/packing recommendations and off-peak discounts rather than broad SKU increases.
- Trial cohort elasticity is noisy; raising price broadly may accelerate churn and reduce long-term conversion; prefer credit-withdrawal (phased) instead of list-price increase.

Immediate next steps (short checklist):
- Finance to validate marginal cost per-1k token by hardware mix (deadline: 2027-02-18) — action: Ravi Kapoor
- Growth to prepare segmented comms for top 200 embedding customers if tilt goes live (deadline: 2027-02-22) — action: Emily Chen
- Product to build usage-tieouts for the hiring freeze trigger (deadline: 2027-02-25) — action: Jonas Muller
- Schedule dry-run of price experiment tracking dashboard in Looker (owner: analytics)

Notes on model fidelity and caveats:
- This sheet intentionally combines coarse elasticity estimates with deterministic hiring costs — treat outputs as directional.
- Does not model multi-account displacement (customers moving to private/dedicated offerings) — a separate run is required before broad price moves.
- Currency FX and regional GPU pricing variance excluded; region-aware version exists as a tab (not yet normalized).

Change log (edits):
- 2026-12-10: initial draft and cohort definitions (S. Nguyen)
- 2027-01-12: updated marginal cost estimates after infra workshop (R. Kapoor)
- 2027-02-10: added hiring-triggers and elasticity sensitivity grid (E. Chen)
